title: [2609.18588] Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: Abstract page: v1 only, submitted 16 Sep 2026, 5 pages, accepted at IEEE PES ISGT Europe 2026. Headline: Chronos-2 has the best high-demand (HD) NMAE and MAPE at all three levels (0.039 and 4.53% area code, 0.080 and 9.45% substation, 0.138 and 16.14% LV feeder), about 20 to 51% below LightGBM and XGBoost on HD-NMAE, best or near-best overall. The page links no code or data.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: Full text, setup: per-meter demand at 30-minute steps for 115 Swiss postal-code areas (CKW), 387 substations and 485 LV feeders (Northern Powergrid); one day-ahead forecast (48 steps) at midnight each, scored 1 Mar 2024 to 28 Feb 2025. High demand = at or above 0.8 of the entity's 99th percentile over the previous 14 days. Authors: FAU Erlangen and Siemens. No code or results repository named.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: Full text, inputs: calendar, holiday and five Open-Meteo weather variables (humidity, feels-like temperature, dew point, wind, solar radiation) are the feature set of LightGBM and XGBoost. The Chronos models are described as forecasting from recent history only (Bolt 2048 steps, Chronos-2 90 days); no covariates are said to reach them. Whether the weather is observed or forecast is not stated.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: Full text, baselines: the boosted trees are not retrained; each season is forecast by a model trained on one fixed earlier 90-day block (winter 2023/24 for spring, autumn and winter; spring 2024 for summer). In the results table both trees have higher overall NMAE than the 7-day same-time average at every level (0.080 vs 0.055 area, 0.098 vs 0.074 substation, 0.115 vs 0.091 feeder).

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: Full text, quantiles: the Chronos rows are not medians. A quantile per level was picked on a small validation set by a rule that weighs the overall NMAE gap to the best non-Chronos model against HD error: q0.65 for Bolt everywhere and for Chronos-2 at area level, q0.70 for Chronos-2 at substation and feeder level. The trees give one point forecast with no such upward shift.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: Results table, HD-NMAE (mean over entities), Chronos-2 / LightGBM / XGBoost / 7-day average: area 0.039 / 0.080 / 0.080 / 0.059; substation 0.080 / 0.113 / 0.113 / 0.117; feeder 0.138 / 0.173 / 0.173 / 0.199. HD-MAPE, Chronos-2 / XGBoost: 4.53 / 9.10, 9.45 / 13.20, 16.14 / 20.02%. Only mean and standard deviation across entities; no intervals or tests.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: Results table, overall: NMAE of Chronos-2 / best other model: area 0.042 / 0.051 (Bolt); substation 0.074 / 0.074 (7-day average); feeder 0.094 / 0.091 (7-day average). Overall MAPE of Chronos-2 is behind the 7-day average at substation (15.81 vs 14.96%) and feeder level (22.80 vs 20.64%); its non-HD NMAE is also above the 7-day average there (0.073 vs 0.068, 0.091 vs 0.082).

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
note: Results text: at feeder level Chronos-2 is 3.3% worse on overall NMAE than the best other model and 30.7% better on HD-NMAE (both figures match the 7-day average, not the trees). Median CPU inference 9.8 s per 24-hour forecast for Chronos-2, 1.3 s for Bolt; 0.2 s and 0.007 s on an A100. The conclusion states about 30% lower HD error than the best non-Chronos models.
